quiz_metadata.title: Tagalog Pronouns Master Quiz (Personal, Demonstrative & Possessive)

questions.prompt: Which pronoun means 'we' EXCLUDING the person being spoken to?
questions.explanation: 'Kami' is the 1st person plural exclusive pronoun (he/she and I, but NOT you).

questions.prompt: Which pronoun means 'we' INCLUDING the person being spoken to?
questions.explanation: 'Tayo' is the 1st person plural inclusive pronoun (you, he/she, and I).

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: _____ ay guro. (I am a teacher)
questions.explanation: 'Ako' is the 1st person singular nominative pronoun ('I').

questions.prompt: When placing the 2nd person singular pronoun AFTER the predicate in inverted order, which form must be used instead of 'Ikaw'?
questions.explanation: 'Ikaw' is used at the beginning of a sentence. After the predicate in inverted order, it shortens to 'ka' (e.g. Mabait ka).

questions.prompt: Which pronoun is gender-neutral and means both 'he' and 'she' in Tagalog?
questions.explanation: Tagalog has no grammatical gender. 'Siya' means both 'he' and 'she'.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence using the polite plural pronoun: _____ po ba ay mag-aaral? (Are you a student, sir/madam?)
questions.explanation: Plural pronouns 'Kayo' or 'Sila' combined with 'po' express politeness when addressing a single person.

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative pronoun refers to an object near the speaker ('this')?
questions.explanation: 'Ito' means 'this' (object near the speaker).

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative pronoun refers to an object near the listener ('that')?
questions.explanation: 'Iyan' means 'that' (object near the person being spoken to).

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative pronoun refers to an object far from BOTH speaker and listener ('that over there')?
questions.explanation: 'Iyon' refers to an object far from both the speaker and listener.

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun corresponding to 1st person singular base 'akin' ('my/mine')?
questions.explanation: Base pre-noun 'akin' (with ligature 'aking') becomes 'ko' when placed after the noun (e.g. ang bahay ko).

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: Ang bahay ___ ay malaki. (My house is big)
questions.explanation: 'Ko' is the 1st person singular post-noun possessive pronoun ('my').

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun corresponding to 2nd person singular base 'iyo' ('your/yours')?
questions.explanation: Base pre-noun 'iyo' (with ligature 'iyong') becomes 'mo' when placed after the noun (e.g. ang baro mo).

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun for 3rd person singular 'kaniya' ('his/her')?
questions.explanation: Pre-noun 'kaniya' becomes 'niya' when placed after the noun (e.g. ang sapatos niya).

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun for 1st person plural EXCLUSIVE ('our' - excluding listener)?
questions.explanation: Pre-noun 'amin' becomes 'namin' when placed after the noun (excludes listener).

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun for 1st person plural INCLUSIVE ('our' - including listener)?
questions.explanation: Pre-noun 'atin' becomes 'natin' when placed after the noun (includes listener).

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun for 3rd person plural 'kanila' ('their/theirs')?
questions.explanation: Pre-noun 'kanila' becomes 'nila' when placed after the noun (e.g. ang lapis nila).

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative possessive word means 'of this' (near speaker)?
questions.explanation: 'Nito' is the possessive form of 'ito' ('of this' near speaker, e.g. ang bahay nito).

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative possessive word means 'of that' (near listener)?
questions.explanation: 'Niyan' is the possessive form of 'iyan' ('of that' near listener).

questions.prompt: When placed BEFORE a noun, what ligature suffix attaches to the base possessive pronoun 'akin'?
questions.explanation: 'Akin' ends in consonant 'n', so it takes the ligature suffix '-g' to become 'aking' (e.g. ang aking bahay).

questions.prompt: Translate to Tagalog: 'Their car is old' (using post-noun possessive): Luma ang kotse _____.
questions.explanation: 'Nila' is the 3rd person plural post-noun possessive pronoun meaning 'their'.
